business_model.basis: Stated in the 10-K Business section (P1) and repeated in the 10-Q MD&A (P4)
business_model.claim: Globalstar provides Mobile Satellite Services (MSS) including voice, data, and IoT communications to retail, business, and governmental customers, as well as wholesale satellite capacity services, over its LEO satellite constellation and global gateway network.
quotes: Through its global satellite network, Globalstar, Inc. ("we," "us" or the "Company") provides Mobile Satellite Services ("MSS"), including voice and data communications services to retail, business and governmental customers as well as wholesale satellite capacity services.

business_model.basis: Stated in the 10-Q MD&A (P4) and 10-K Risk Factors (P2)
business_model.claim: Wholesale satellite capacity services to Apple Inc. under the Updated Services Agreements constitute the dominant revenue source, accounting for 64% of total revenue in the nine months ended September 30, 2026.
quotes: For the nine months ended September 30, 2026 and 2025, the Customer under the Updated Services Agreements was responsible for 64% and 63%, respectively, of our total revenue.

business_model.basis: Stated in the 8-K earnings release (P6) and reflected in the 10-Q income statement (F2)
business_model.claim: Revenue is reported in two categories: service revenue (subdivided into wholesale capacity services, Commercial IoT, SPOT, Duplex, and government/other services) and subscriber equipment sales.
quotes: Total revenue for the third quarter of 2026 was $70.9 million, including $65.4 million of service revenue and $5.5 million of revenue generated from subscriber equipment sales.

business_model.basis: Stated in the 10-K MD&A (P3) for activations; subscriber table in the 8-K release (P6)
business_model.claim: Commercial IoT is the fastest-growing subscriber segment, with gross activations up over 50% year over year to a record high, and average subscribers rising from 542,715 in Q3 2025 to 591,114 in Q3 2026.
quotes: Gross subscriber activations were up over 50% year over year, reaching a record high for annual gross activations since our Commercial IoT devices were first introduced.

business_model.basis: Stated in the 10-K MD&A (P3); subscriber trends confirmed in the 8-K release (P6)
business_model.claim: SPOT and Duplex subscriber services are in structural decline: SPOT revenue fell $3.8 million in 2025 due to competitive pressure, and Duplex revenue fell $4.9 million after the company discontinued manufacture and sale of Duplex devices.
quotes: SPOT service revenue decreased $3.8 million in 2025 due to fewer subscribers, and to a lesser extent, a slight decrease in ARPU.

Duplex service revenue decreased $4.9 million in 2025 due to fewer average subscribers resulting from our decision to discontinue the manufacture and sale of Duplex devices to increase our focus on maximizing other sources of revenue.

business_model.basis: Stated in the 10-Q income statement (F2) and explained in the 10-K MD&A (P3)
business_model.claim: Interest expense is the single largest non-operating cost, with net interest income and expense of $64,384 (table in thousands) for the nine months ended September 30, 2026, driven by the Infrastructure Prepayment financing component and the 2024 Debt Repayment accrued fees.
quotes: Interest income and expense, net, increased $27.3 million to $40.9 million for 2025 compared to $13.6 million for 2024.

business_model.basis: Stated in the 10-K MD&A (P3); 9M 2026 investing cash flows of $(414,226) (table in thousands) in the 10-Q cash flow statement (F3) confirm ongoing heavy capex
business_model.claim: Capital expenditures for the Extended MSS Network (new C-3 satellite constellation and ground infrastructure) represent the primary use of investing cash, with $708.6 million incurred of a $1.5 billion projected spend as of December 31, 2025, all funded by prepayments from Apple.
quotes: As of December 31, 2025, we have incurred $708.6 million of the $1.5 billion projected spend for the Extended MSS Network, all of which to date has been funded with prepayments from the Customer.

business_model.claim: Globalstar retains 15% of its current and future network capacity for its own subscribers and potential other wholesale customers, providing a path to grow the subscriber-driven portion of revenue.
quotes: We retain 15% of our current and future network capacity to support our other customers, including our existing and future Commercial IoT, SPOT and Duplex subscribers.

business_model.basis: Stated in the 10-Q MD&A (P4); terrestrial spectrum revenue contribution is small (4,018 (table in thousands) for 9M 2026 per P6)

business_model.basis: Stated in the 10-Q MD&A (P4), 10-Q Risk Factors (P5), and 8-K earnings release (P6)
business_model.claim: A pending acquisition by Amazon.com, Inc. (agreement signed April 13, 2026) is expected to close in 2027, subject to remaining regulatory approvals and HIBLEO-4 satellite milestones; if the deal fails, Globalstar could owe a termination fee of approximately $420 million.
quotes: The Mergers are expected to close in 2027, subject to satisfaction of certain closing conditions in the Merger Agreement, including required regulatory approvals; however, no assurance can be given as to when, or if, the Mergers will occur.

For the years ended December 31, 2025, 2024 and 2023, the Customer under the Updated Services Agreements was responsible for 63%, 58%, and 49%, respectively, of our total revenue.

("XCOM") to purchase intellectual property assets relating to the development and commercialization of XCOM's technologies for wireless spectrum innovations, including XCOM RAN systems, which is XCOM's commercially available coordinated multi-point radio system.
